la:noun:fautor.html:
fautor (uncontr. făvĭtor, Lucil. ap. ; and 79; , acc. to Cod. Erf.), ōris, m.
faveo
,
a favorer, furtherer, promoter, maintainer, patron (class.).
With gen.: cujus ego dignitatis ab adulescentia fautor (with adjutor),; cf. fin.; 12, 25, 3: multi fautores laudis tuae,; cf.: studiosi et fautores illius victoriae,: nobilitatis,; clamor ab utriusque fautoribus oritur,from the partisans,: competitorum,: regis,: et cultor bonorum (populus),: inepte (i. q. inepte favens) Lucili,; cf. veterum,: omnes illi fautores illius flagitii,: nequitiae,.—
With dat.: favitorem tibi me, amicum, amatorem putes, Lucil. ap. : aetati facieque tuae se Fautorem ostendat, id. ap. : cum tam multos et bonos viros ejus (Plancii) honori viderem esse favitores, etc.,.—
Absol.: virtute ambire oportet, non favitoribus: Sat habet favitorum semper, qui recte facit,i. e. applauders, claqueurs,; so ; ; .

la:noun:fauces.gloss: the upper part of a throat; pharynx; gullet
senses: the upper part of a throat; pharynx; gullet
a narrow entrance; entry passage; defile; gorge; the jaws of the earth; gulf; abyss
la:noun:fauces.html:
fauces, ium (
sing. nom. faux only in , =arteria aspera; cf. Müll.; P. —The abl. sing. fauce sometimes in poets: ; ; ; ; ; ), f.
cf. Sanscr. bhūka, hole, opening
, the upper part of the throat, from the root of the tongue to the entrance of the gullet, the pharynx, throat, gullet (syn.: gula, guttur, jugulum).
Lit.: summum gulae fauces vocantur, extremum stomachus; quibus fauces non sunt, ne stomachus quidem est,: exigua in arteria sub ipsis faucibus lingula est, quae, cum spiramus, attollitur,: (galli) favent faucibus russis cantu, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 250 ed. Vahl.): sitis fauces tenet,: sitis fauces urit,: lippiunt fauces fame,; : fauces tussientes,: nuces videntur fauces exasperare,: fauces tumentes strangulant vocem, etc.,: infirmatis faucibus, praeconis voce concionatus est,: propino tibi salutem plenis faucibus,: merum ingurgitare faucibus plenis,: exscrea usque ex penitis faucibus,from the bottom of your throat,: alicui fauces prehendere,; cf.: qui sacerdoti scelestus fauces interpresserit,: laqueo innectere fauces,to strangle,; cf. also: ad necem secandasque novacula fauces,: fauces manu sua oppressit,: retinens singulos et contortis faucibus convertens,.—Trop.: faucibus teneor,I am caught by the throat, I feel the knife at my throat,; cf.: cum faucibus premeretur,: Timarchides premit fauces defensionis tuae,: eripite nos ex faucibus eorum, quorum crudelitas, etc., from the jaws, Crass. ap. ; cf. : urbem totius belli ore ac faucibus ereptam esse,: e mediis Orci faucibus ad hunc evasi modum,: cum inexplebiles populi fauces exaruerunt libertatis siti,: lupus fauce improba incitatus,i. e. voracity,.—
Transf., of places:
A narrow way, narrow inlet or outlet, an entrance, defile, pass (cf. angustiae): Corinthus posita in angustiis atque in faucibus Graeciae, in the mouth or entrance, : in Ciliciae angustissimis faucibus,; cf.: qua fauces erant angustissimae portus,: portus,; 3, 39, 2: Masinissam persecutus in valle arta, faucibus utrimque obsessis, inclusit,: Aemilius sedens in faucibus macelli,; so, macelli,: per fauces montis ut Aetnae Exspirent ignes,the crater,: cava flumina siccis faucibus, etc.,: altae montis,: Nilus multis faucibus in Aegyptium mare se evomit,through many mouths,: Bospori,the Dardanelles,, § 4; : cum fornacem facies, fauces praecipites deorsum facito,: pictis e faucibus currus emittere, from the barriers, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 89 ed. Vahl.).—
The jaws of the earth, gulf, abyss: patefactis terrae faucibus,.

la:noun:Faunus.html:
Faunus, i, m.
faveo
,
a mythic son of Picus, grandson of Saturn, and father of Latinus, king of Latium; he instituted tillage and grazing, and after death was the protecting deity of agriculture and of shepherds, and also a giver of oracles; after the introduction of the worship of Pan into Italy, he was identified with Pan, and accordingly represented, like the latter, with horns and goats' feet, ; ; ; ; ; sq.; ; ; ; ; et saep. On account of the assimilation of Faunus to Pan, the appellation Fauni was also used for Panes, sylvan deities, ; ; ; ; ; Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 222 ed. Vahl.); ; .—
Derivv.
Faunĭus, a, um, adj., pertaining to Faunus: versus, Victorinn. p. 2586 P.—
† Faunālĭa, ium, n., the festival celebrated on the nones of December, in honor of Faunus, acc. to Porphyr. and Acro, and 10.

la:noun:Fauna.html:
Fauna, ae, f.,
the prophesying sister of Faunus, called also Bona Dea, ; ; .

la:adj:faustus.html:
faustus, a, um, adj.
for favostus, from faveo; lit., favorable; hence
,
of favorable or fortunate omen, fortunate, favorable, auspicious, prosperous, lucky (rare but class.; cf.: felix, fortunatus, beatus, prosperus, dexter, secundus): quae (omina) majores nostri quia valere censebant, idcirco omnibus rebus agendis: QVOD BONVM FAVSTVM FELIX FORTVNATVMQVE ESSET praefabantur,: so, ut nobis haec habitatio Bona, fausta, felix fortunataque eveniat,: utile sit faustumque precor, quod imagine somni Vidimus,: omen,; ; ; cf.: exitus ut classi felix faustusque daretur,: i pede fausto,: indoles Nutrita faustis sub penetralibus,: o faustum et felicem hunc diem!; cf. : o nox illa fausta huic urbi!: annus,: nisi tempestas indulget tempore fausto,favorable, suitable,.—Hence, * fauste, adv., favorably, fortunately: ut eis quoque hominibus ea res fauste, feliciter prospereque eveniret,.
